Your strawberry frosting containing FD&C Red No. 3 must stop being manufactured with that color additive by January 15, 2027. On that date, the removal of 21 CFR 74.303 (the listing authorizing FD&C Red No. 3 in food) takes effect, and all existing certificates for batches of FD&C Red No. 3 cease to be effective for use in food (90 FR 4628; 91 FR 50475). The administrative stay that was in place from February 18, 2025, was lifted on August 5, 2026, and the January 15, 2027 effective date was confirmed (91 FR 50475).

Regarding product already on shelves: The January 2025 order explicitly states that '[w]hen FD&C Red No. 3 has been used in food or ingested drugs while its certificate is still effective, such food or ingested drugs will not be regarded as adulterated by reason of the use of such color additive' (90 FR 4628). This means frosting manufactured and containing FD&C Red No. 3 that was incorporated while the certificate was still effective (i.e., before January 15, 2027) is NOT adulterated and may remain on shelves and be sold after that date. Only use of FD&C Red No. 3 after its certificate ceases to be effective (i.e., incorporating it into food on or after January 15, 2027) would render the food adulterated.

Note: The January 2025 order sets no separate compliance date; the operative deadline is derived from the effective date of January 15, 2027. There is no phase-out period or sell-through deadline beyond that distinction between when the color additive was incorporated into the food.

response.answer:
Under the updated 'healthy' nutrient content claim rule (89 FR 106064, codified at 21 CFR 101.65(d)), a food that does not qualify for one of the automatic exemptions (e.g., single-ingredient foods from encouraged food groups, or water/tea/coffee) must meet two main criteria to bear the 'healthy' claim:

1. **Food Group Equivalent (FGE) requirement**: The food must contain a specified amount of at least one food group equivalent from the food groups encouraged by the Dietary Guidelines (vegetables, fruits, whole grains, fat-free or low-fat dairy, lean meat/seafood/eggs/beans/peas/lentils/nuts/seeds). The specific FGE amounts vary by product category (individual food, mixed product, main dish, or meal) as set forth in 21 CFR 101.65(d)(3)(ii)–(v) and the associated tables. (21 CFR 101.65(d)(2)–(3); 89 FR 106064)

2. **Nutrient-to-Limit (NTL) requirement**: The food must not exceed specified limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium, expressed as a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients. These limits also vary by product category. (21 CFR 101.65(d)(3)(ii)–(v); 89 FR 106064; see also 90 FR 10592 at passage describing the rule as requiring 'FGEs and specific limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium based on a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients')

As summarized in the background section of 90 FR 10592 (Doc. 2025-03118): the rule 'requires that, to bear a claim subject to the rule, individual food products, mixed products, main dishes, and meals must meet FGEs and specific limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium based on a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients.'

response.answer:
No, that was not a fair reading in mid-2025, and it is definitively incorrect now.

**What was true in mid-2025:** The January 2025 order revoking FD&C Red No. 3 (90 FR 4628, published 2025-01-16, Doc. 2025-00830) was subject to an automatic administrative stay under 21 U.S.C. 371(e)(2) as of February 18, 2025, triggered by the filing of objections. During that stay, the effective dates of January 15, 2027 (food uses, removal of 21 CFR 74.303) and January 18, 2028 (ingested drugs, removal of 21 CFR 74.1303) were suspended but not cancelled or moved. The order itself was a final binding order, not a proposal. An administrative stay does not mean a rule 'might never take effect'—it means the agency must evaluate the objections before the rule can proceed. The stated effective dates remained on the books, albeit unconfirmed during the stay period.

Saying the removal was 'not final' mischaracterized the legal posture: the January 2025 order was a final order issued under section 721(d) of the FD&C Act (90 FR 4628). The stay was a statutory procedural consequence of objections being filed, not a sign of legal infirmity or uncertainty about finality.

**What is the position now:** FDA published a document on August 5, 2026 (91 FR 50475, Doc. 2026-15920) that overrules all objections, denies requests for a public hearing, lifts the administrative stay, and explicitly confirms the effective dates of January 15, 2027, and January 18, 2028. The document states: 'we are ending the administrative stay of the January 2025 order, and under the January 2025 order we are repealing the listing for FD&C Red No. 3 in § 74.303 as a color additive in food and § 74.1303 as a color additive in ingested drugs effective January 15, 2027, and January 18, 2028, respectively' (91 FR 50475). This constitutes 'final action on the objections' under section 701(e)(2) of the FD&C Act.

The revocation is therefore fully confirmed and binding. After January 15, 2027, use of FD&C Red No. 3 in food will render such food adulterated (90 FR 4628). No compliance date is separately stated; the operative deadline is derived from the effective date of January 15, 2027 for food uses.

The Red No. 3 order (90 FR 4628, Doc. 2025-00830, published 2025-01-16) changes two CFR provisions in 21 CFR Part 74, but they do NOT all change on the same day:

1. **21 CFR 74.303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for food use): The order removes (revokes) this section entirely. It also revises 21 CFR 74.1303 to incorporate the identity and specifications language from § 74.303(a)(1) and (b), since § 74.1303 previously cross-referenced § 74.303 for those details. Both the removal of § 74.303 and the interim revision of § 74.1303 become effective **January 15, 2027** (amendatory instructions 2 and 3). (90 FR 4628; passage 2025-00830#0002; passage 2025-00830#0000)

2. **21 CFR 74.1303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for ingested drugs): The order removes this section entirely, effective **January 18, 2028** (amendatory instruction 4). (90 FR 4628; passage 2025-00830#0002; passage 2025-00830#0000)

Thus the order has two different effective dates. The administrative stay that began February 18, 2025, was lifted August 5, 2026, and both effective dates (January 15, 2027, and January 18, 2028) are confirmed without change (91 FR 50475, Doc. 2026-15920).

No separate compliance date is stated in either document. Because this is a revocation (not a new affirmative requirement), the operative deadline for each provision is derived from its effective date: after that date the listing is gone and any food or drug containing FD&C Red No. 3 is adulterated. (90 FR 4628, passage 2025-00830#0021)

response.answer: Under 21 CFR 101.65(a)(2), a 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim must be made in accordance with the general requirements for nutrient content claims in § 101.13, with one specific carve-out: § 101.13(h) is excepted when the nutrient content claim is made in accordance with paragraph (d) of § 101.65. Section 101.13(h) is the disclosure requirement that would otherwise mandate a statement such as 'See nutrition information for ___ content' when a food exceeds specified levels of fat, saturated fat, cholesterol, or sodium. This carve-out means that a food bearing the 'healthy' claim under § 101.65(d) is not required to include the § 101.13(h) disclosure statement, even if the food would otherwise trigger it. All other provisions of § 101.13 (e.g., type size requirements in (f), general claim requirements in (b), substitute food provisions in (d), etc.) remain applicable to a 'healthy' claim.

response.answer: Yes, your shelf-stable lentil soup labeled 'healthy' is affected by the updated definition of the term 'healthy' under the final rule published at 89 FR 106064 (Doc. 2024-29957, published 2024-12-27). This rule revises 21 CFR 101.65(d) to establish new food-group-equivalent (FGE) and nutrient-to-limit (NTL) criteria for foods bearing the 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim.
